title: Secure Global Microservice Delivery
business: Global e-commerce retailers requiring low-latency, secure access to distributed microservices.
problem: High latency and exposure of backend microservice endpoints to the public internet, leading to performance degradation and increased attack surface.
solution: Utilizing Azure Front Door to provide a scalable, security-enhanced delivery point that terminates SSL/TLS at the edge and routes traffic to backend microservices hosted on Azure Container Apps.
steps: Deploy microservices as containerized applications using Azure Container Apps.
Configure Azure Front Door as the global entry point for all web traffic.
Implement Private Link to establish a private, secure connection between the Front Door edge and the internal container environment.
Define routing rules in Front Door to direct traffic based on URL paths to specific microservice endpoints.
outcome: Improved global application performance through edge caching and reduced latency, combined with a hardened security posture by masking backend infrastructure.
limitation: The primary limitation is the complexity of managing global routing rules and certificate lifecycle across multiple origins. Check this by monitoring the Azure Front Door health reports and backend response times in Azure Monitor.

The complexity of managing global routing rules and certificate lifecycle.

questions.evidence: The primary limitation is the complexity of managing global routing rules and certificate lifecycle across multiple origins.
